sections.title: Narrating an event clearly: meaning and form
body: Goal: Tell a short, coherent story with a beginning, turning point, response and outcome.
Core vocabulary: en händelse, plötsligt, till slut. Key phrases: Först väntade jag vid hållplatsen. · Plötsligt märkte jag att väskan var borta. · Till slut fick jag tillbaka den.

Use preterite for the chain of completed events and past perfect, hade + supine, for something already completed before another past event. Time markers such as först, sedan, plötsligt and till slut guide the listener through the story.
Say the examples aloud, notice the pattern, and then change one detail rather than memorising a fixed script.

sections.title: Register, evidence and independent use
body: Register model: “Sedan upptäckte jag att jag hade lämnat den hemma.” is a neutral narrative way to express “Then I discovered that I had left it at home.”.
For listening and reading, answer from a specific word or phrase. For speaking and writing, make the recipient, purpose and next action clear.
Attempt the task before using the model. Improve one high-impact feature, then perform it again with the transfer condition.

assignment.title: Four-skill task and transfer
assignment.instructions:
LISTEN: First listen without a transcript. Answer: Where had the speaker put the keys? Replay once and identify the exact words that prove the answer.

READ: Read for purpose and evidence. Answer: Why did Tuva stop under a bridge? Mark the shortest phrase that supports your choice.

SPEAK: Tell a 60–90 second original story about a small everyday problem. Include the setting, a surprising turn, what you did and the outcome. Make a first attempt, check clarity and repeat once.

WRITE: Write a 100-word narrative about missing, losing or misunderstanding something. Use sequence markers and at least one hade + supine form. Check reader, purpose, required details and next action.

TRANSFER: Retell the same event to a service worker who only needs the facts relevant to solving the problem.

BETWEEN LESSON · Optional, 5 minutes: retrieve the three key phrases without looking, then use one in a new sentence.
